execution.method: single-leg limit orders: buy both wings first, then sell the body legs. To close: buy back the shorts first, then sell the wings. Never sell a wing while its short leg is open.
execution.approval: single-leg orders need no customer approval while human_must_approve_trades=false
execution.deep_itm_note: A short leg that is deep in the money cannot be bought back alone when its price is above the buying power (NVDA 175P on 2026-11-12: $1,545 against $994 at the open). Such a spread is held at its max loss (v1.2.2) until the short leg's ask x 100 is inside the buying power, then closed short leg first, with the wing sold at once as a marketable limit.

why_not_cut: Robinhood refused the 4-leg closing order (4.65 debit) at 06:41 PT: 'this account requires the customer to approve agent-placed trades, and a multi-leg strategy cannot be sent for approval yet'.

Single legs do not work here: buying back the 175 put costs about $1,545 and buying power is $994 (the collateral only comes back once the 175 call is closed too, and that still leaves it about $80 short).

Even with the buying power, legging out means holding the long 170 put alone (worth about $1,100, $80 per $1 in NVDA) between the two orders, in a stock moving $1 a minute. That adds more risk than the cut removes.
The position is already near its max loss: a close at the mid saves about $35 against the worst case and gives up the roughly 1 in 8 chance that NVDA is back inside 171.16 to 178.84 on Friday.
